Reorder columns of a GPU table

Source: R/relocate.R
relocate.tbl_gpu.Rd

Moves columns of a GPU table to a new position, similar to dplyr::relocate(). The reorder runs on the GPU as a column selection, like select.tbl_gpu(); a rename (relocate(df, a = x)) only changes the column names, like rename.tbl_gpu().

Usage

# S3 method for class 'tbl_gpu'
relocate(.data, ..., .before = NULL, .after = NULL)

Arguments

.data

A tbl_gpu object created by tbl_gpu().

...

Columns to move (tidyselect syntax; may include new = old renames).

.before, .after

Destination, as a tidyselect specification of an existing column; the selected columns are placed immediately before/ after it. At most one of .before/.after may be supplied; if neither is given, selected columns move to the front.

Value

A tbl_gpu object with columns reordered (and any requested columns renamed).

Examples

library(dplyr)
if (has_gpu()) {
  gpu_mtcars <- tbl_gpu(mtcars)

  result <- gpu_mtcars |>
    relocate(hp, .after = mpg) |>
    collect()
}
